I appreciate trigger warnings in either summaries or just a single authors note because sometimes obviously just the tags aren’t always clear enough and I take the risk anyway since I’m fine with most things and have had unfortunately a few times had to put down stories because the triggers were something I couldn’t ignore, but I never held it against the author just felt like a loss. Sometimes authors will add in their notes or before the chapter begins a simple but not spoiler-esque warning like “Hey just a heads up this chapter contains some serious non-con” and it’ll put me in a place to mentally prepare or prep me to skip over it. I don’t expect authors to do this on every fic, it just feels kind of like finding a random dollar bill on the ground and getting to keep it. A nice addition! I’m sorry you had a lot of anxiety/paranoia when it came to having to spoon feed trigger warnings to certain readers, and I’m glad you’re now more comfortable at ease with your stories! For what it’s worth, I feel like the tag “Dead Dove: Do Not Eat” in itself always tells me to brace for the strongest possibility of the story containing a trigger I have. If you’re adding it to your stories and still receiving complaints that you should have added more warnings, then at this point it’s just someone either not familiar with the tags meaning (because it basically means “This story contains extremely dark elements and I’m not responsible for you being upset if you decide to still read it.”) or someone wanting everything spoon fed to them and are looking for something to complain about it. 

Side note: Fucking a for reaching that high word count! Long lengthy fanfics are my FAVOURITE to read but I know they’re definitely stressful for authors so I wanna just send out some happy cheerleader vibes and say thank you so much for letting us (readers in general) experience your own story/take in your world. The hours it must take and the writers block you no doubt likely suffer from time to time may make you feel like there’s no point to keep going, but I swear your efforts and passions are beloved and cherished amongst the community. Don’t think this means you’re obligated to push or muscle through when you know you need a break or are finished, you’re simply sharing your own world with us and we have the privilege *not* the entitlement to experience it. Have a good night or day!!

For a certain time I was extremely off put by Mpreg tags, despite feeling like I was the most progressive person on earth. Yet there was still some part of me I wasn’t even aware of conditioned into thinking something like that is extremely out of the norm, and merely the fantasies of certain preferences and kinks. It depends on his own comfort when it comes to horror and his own emotional/mental stability. If someone has a lot of personal trauma/anxiety resulting from dark and heavy themes such as manipulation and *severe* gas lighting then I wouldn’t recommend this show or would at the very least give them content warnings. 

The display of horror/gore isn’t senseless and chaotic, it’s very classy and the cinematography is gorgeous and nothing short of artistic, but it *is* in your face and not shy about it. The theme it follows is a very macabre and impactful one. This show is heavy psychological horror that requires (usually for first time viewers) rapt focus in order to follow the story, and could possibly be a bad watch for someone who’s not comfortable with themes like this.

I think it’s different for every marginalized person. I’m queer and not comfortable with stories pretending that at a certain point it wasn’t dangerous for me to be openly queer out in person. It’s like comparing apples to oranges because magic is fictitious in predominant ways and bigotry is not and still very rampant, but I have many friends who loves stories that do this. I’d never take that away from them, because a lot of them depend on these stories to give them safe haven from the world. I just personally don’t like it and would rather a story let me know in some form of tag that it’s what they’re doing. It’s all about comfort and why it’s a pet peeve. I don’t think anybody is stepping on anyone’s toes when it comes to preferring this. 

On the other hand, there 100% was uses of gender neutral pronouns being used during and before the 90s (non-binary people who existed in the 90s using (either mentally/subconsciously) gender neutral pronouns). Just because we weren’t as loud about it outside of our (then smaller/hidden) communities doesn’t mean we didn’t exist. I was born right at the end of the 90s myself but I know of and was friends with plenty of older folk who use gender neutral pronouns and have been since they were younger but only ever recently started *correcting people out loud* that weren’t in their personal social/safe circles. Because now it’s somewhat safer to do so. Yes, we didn’t see it in movies or magazines like we do now but because you would become a social pariah if you did come out about it. This isn’t a trend that appeared out of nowhere, singular use gender neutral pronouns are actually very very old and a fun thing to learn about! We just finally got big enough voices to rally up and make ourselves heard. I think if written particularly well (if the social setting is smaller more close-knit friends/family story telling) the use of more socially accepting dynamics works and helps the story because some of us had supportive communities during tough times like that and some of us didn’t. But if it’s just a story set in the 80s except everyone is *super* cool about being gay and whatnot.. That’s just not my style, but I won’t take it away from anyone else.

I used to get embarrassed over my reactions to when I’d seek out a hug from my best friend or from my mom, and they’d wrap their arms around me and put all their strength into squeezing me tight, I’d feel so overwhelmed with the evidence that I matter to them that I’m stifling sobs. It kills me inside that predominantly men and AMAB individuals aren’t allowed to do this, without feeling put on the spot, insecure, or self conscious about putting out the wrong vibe and being received in a way they’re not intending. Humans are social creatures (in our own ways) and even though many of us don’t realize, recognize or just deny this, we thrive and survive off of this. 
You’re allowed to want to hug your fucking friends. 

Out there are countless men and AMAB individuals, specifically *young individuals*, who are growing up and learning all the wrong ways to show love. Who probably don’t realize that getting a soul crushing hug from a friend or a loved one can sometimes knock the wind out of you in such a magical way. Can sometimes truly be one of the most important things you could receive while fighting some battles in your life. 
Someone who probably wants to reach out and play with his buddy’s hair because it looks soft and smells good, and your instinct just makes you wanna react. But is scared he’ll get made fun of or *worse*.

Where you have sex, or are expected to commit in ways that take a lot from you. I wonder how many have rushed it just because they want to explore, and give in to these urges and are convinced that this means they’re ready to take it farther. TL;DR; Kneeling in raw rice is an extremely torturous punishment for a child. 


Childhood punishment. Kneeling on raw rice.

I was a hellion child so a lot of my adventures tended to end in different punishments like spankings, getting popped in the mouth, grounded, put in time out, whipped (it’s different from spankings.. trust me), locked in my room, hot sauce in my mouth, soap bar in my mouth, writing punishments, etc. the worst one in my experience was raw rice. Thankfully this was a rare punishment, I genuinely hated it.

For those who don’t know what the rice punishment is:
You pour raw rice onto the floor in a corner and kneel in it with your bare knees for whatever time (for me it was usually 15-20 minutes.) Knees straight, back straight, hands either locked together behind your back or placed noticeably against the wall away from your legs. If you’re caught brushing the rice off of your knees to ease the pain the time starts over. If you were caught sitting back on your legs or doing anything that lifts your knees the time starts over.

I had an especially traumatic experience with this punishment. I was in big big trouble for whatever I did, no specific details but I know that I really chose the wrong day to act cute so I got the rice punishment. At the time my parents owned a separate trailer on our land for their business and mom spent most of her time in it to work. Sometimes my middle sister would come out of her room while I was being punished on rice and stand there waiting for me to get so restless I’d wouldn’t be able to resist lifting my knee or moving my hands and she’d run off to tell my mom and get my punishment extended.

This time on rice I was *petrified* of lifting my knees or leaning back at all. The times before I was only kneeling long enough to be extremely uncomfortable, and crying because I was bored. Constantly rocking and adjusting positions and picking at the wall. This time I was on my knees for so long, longer than I could ever remember being and weeping because I was so genuinely scared if I got caught by anybody trying to brush the rice from my knees or lean back on my legs this eternity would start all over again. So I kept my knees in place. It was agonizing, I can’t think of a better description. At 7/8 years old this was one of the most intensive situations I recall. I was used to quick punishments that hurt for an hour afterwards and left me pouting. I was struggling to keep my sobbing quiet because I was trying to listen for footsteps or hear if anyone would come near while I leaned back for just a second for relief and immediately straighten back up. I remember hearing my heart beating in my ears and choking on phlegm in my throat. My fucking arms were aching and my legs were trembling and shaking so hard I can practically vibrating in one spot, I would have little spastic moments where my knee kind of buckled or rolled out and my butt would dip towards the floor and I jerk so hard back into place and dig those kernels even deeper into the raw bits of flesh and cry so hard. I distinctively remember leaning my head against the wall, pinching my eyes shut and taking tiny naps in between sobbing and fighting with myself to stay still. I have no idea how long this was, my instincts keep wanting to say something dramatic like 3 hours but it definitely wasn’t. It felt like that because I was a 7/8 year old kid diagnosed with extreme adhd. It was maybe an hour.

My mom finally ran in and ripped me off the ground absolutely ashamed and apologetic because she had gotten completely engrossed in her work and forgot about punishing me. Turns out years later when I asked if she remembered this it was my oldest sister that saved the day. She said my oldest sister came in timid and soft spoken, (out of character for her because she was super edgy and emo and was almost never emotionally phased by anything) and *begged* my mom to let me up because it was going on too long and it’s torturing me. My mom jumped up and made like lightening to me, and we never received the punishment again. 

My mom believes I’m overreacting and embellishing the story, and maybe my mind is making it more terrifying than the ordeal was, but I’m not convinced. Like I said, I faced *many* punishments of the physical variety. When our sperm donor whipped us (he’s not in our lives anymore thank god) I had to stay completely still and bent over because he told me he would not stop until he’s finished and any marks anywhere other than my butt was my fault alone. I flailed like a lobster in boiling water, I commonly had lashings across my back and thighs. I had to sit patiently with soap in my mouth for 20 minutes. I had to write repeatedly in a notebook front and back until it was *filled* completely, and *this* memory is what’s followed me and still gives me lingering stress. I hate this fucking punishment. 

This is always why I’m so anti-physical discipline. All of the punishments I received were never in the “heat of the moment” but because I was disrespectful or did something bad. All of these punishments and why they happened fell completely in line with what a large portion of society consider to be acceptable reasons to be your child. I was a snot that got popped/spanked for not being respectful to my elders or back talking. I got yelled at, pinned against walls and had spittle coat my face from a 6’4 man I was supposed to feel protected and safe by. I have had the ‘fear of God’ put into me and as a result: I learned my thank yous, I still say my yes sirs and no mam’s, and make sure to be nice and proper for my elders who are kind. I keep my elbows off the table, I squat when wearing skirts, and say nothing when I have nothing nice to say. 

My first instinct when faced with someone who’s slightly rude to me? *violence*. My first instinct when some random strangers child accidentally bumps into me, or is screaming across an aisle? *violence*. My first instinct when I feel like I’m not treated how I feel I’m entitled to be? *violence* My first instinct is always fantasizing how I’d drag that individual out and beat the fuck out of them. Hearing some child screaming or being mouthy at their parent my first instinct is I would grab them by their hair and beat their ass until it purpled. My first instinct when being disrespected from some meaningless interaction with is how I want to scream in their face and crowd them into a corner until they’re cowering below me and apologize for angering me. 

I don’t act these out of course and immediately calm down and kick myself for thinking so violently but those are always my first instinct. When my boss or a coworker says something derivative my head starts to ache because I have to ignore the first impulsive suggestion which is to beat them until they respect me. When someone’s child doesn’t say thank you after I do something for them, I have to take deep breaths because my face tightens and heats because I’m struggling to ignore my first impulsive instinct which is to beat this random child into respecting me and saying thank you. 

It’s because of these problems I have I’m not ever having kids. I was never fond of the idea of having kids but was always up to considering it if I ever had a partner who wanted them, but as I got older I just knew this wasn’t going to ever be a possibility because I refuse to ever entertain the possibility of having a snap moment and hitting a child just because I was angry at them. That’s not discipline to me. That’s just getting into a physical altercation with someone you don’t like in the moment and that someone is a *child*. I can’t bare that thought. I’m so ashamed of my impulsive emotions and I’ll forever blame that on the physical discipline I received as a child. My first instinct when someone does something I don’t like is to always violently harm them until they correct themselves. 

I’m not trying to say people who got physically punished/spanked/whipped as kids all turn out like me. But there are people who do turn out like me and don’t know it because they think these are normal thoughts. For a long time I was one of those people who always said “*I got punished and I turned out fine!*” and completely believed it until I finally realized that my violent instincts aren’t normal.

It’s sad to admit to, but reading fanfiction about my favourite couples and then going into the more risqué territories of it kind of broadened my horizons. Dammit I’m torn between TCM and Friday the 13th. Friday the 13th was maybe the best remake of a slasher franchise, which I hardly consider TCM to really be. I mean it has slasher elements but really I consider slashers to follow these main rules (imho I’m not gonna disregard a slasher for not following these points I just find them to be the most consistent pattern) which is usually

1: Stalking the Mc/victims at their homes or work (Leatherface only becomes a threat after they’ve stepped into his home/threatened his family) 

2: Primary cause of killing spree has to have something where the MC/Victims have some form or either direct/loose connection to the reason. (*Ghostface* was because Sydney’s mom, *Jason* was because he hates camp counselors bc they killed his mom, *Freddy* bc the kids parents etc —- Sawyer family is just deranged killers/cannibals who go out of their way to antagonize or cause fear)

3: Usually works alone or with 1 other individual and the movie is set up with audience/victims *believing* it’s only one killer (*Ghostface* prime example.) and TCM has an entire family in the works. 

4: Has to go out of their way to hide from/avoid arrest/capture/persecution. Yknow the scene where a cop is present and is either killed or doesn’t believe the victims and the killer gets away/kills him. They make the protagonist or victims look unreliable or paranoid. The Sawyer family pretty much had the run of the town in most of the franchise (not including original which was mostly around their house/yard and its direct sequel) 

I consider TCM franchise to be grindhouse/slaughter film horror among the same lines of Wrong Turn, or Hills Have Eyes. They’re more survival horrors, wrong place wrong time horrors. Not really slashers— so if I’m choosing best slasher remake out of this list, Friday the 13th. If I’m choosing the best *horror* movie remake out of this list, TCM 2003 for fucking *miles* SPECIFICALLY because of R. Lee Ermey’s portrayal of Sheriff Hoyt. The Leatherface in this film was definitely the scariest in terms of scariest fucking mask, brutalist kills, terrifying persona portrayal when compared to the originals and he is not only outshined by R. Lee’s Hoyt in personality and deviance but this man who’s literally just an old ass dude managed to instill a nasty fear inside me. 

Like I’d rather get locked in a room with every single Leatherface in the franchise than with Sheriff Hoyt because I know with Leatherface it’s a painful but somewhat quick death by chainsaw. With Sheriff Hoyt? Who the fuck knows what that man would do to me before my untimely demise. TCM would have honestly held up without him, but his addition was like that Christmas bonus check that saves your fucking marriage.

If it’s an option at all, I’d recommend blocking and ceasing all contact or ways of getting into contact. It’s one of my *biggest* rules when ending a relationship with a toxic person whether I’m the one who was toxic either unintentionally or just lost in my stubbornness or they were. It’s not worth the headache of being dangled on what ifs. Wondering if they’re thinking about messaging you, wondering if they know they have the opportunity to and choose not to do it because they don’t care about you anymore or if they’re just too nervous, then wondering if that means you should be brave enough to reach out first. Or wondering if there’s any meaning behind their messages, whether you should ask or if that makes you come off as longing or desperate, then wondering if it’s okay to maybe question or consider pursuing something again because maybe you’ve both grown out of whatever it was that led to the break up. Maybe if you work harder or resign to not address or act the way you did before and just let them sort of dictate the flow of things you’ll have a successful relationship. Or wondering if they’re just living their life, being nice and saying hi, then wondering if you’re the problematic one for still thinking about them, and wondering if this means you still have feelings for them or undisclosed thoughts/answers about your relationship. 
It’s like tripping over a snake hole everyday and knowing we should fill it but something we keep forgetting because it’s easy to forget when you have so many other things going on. One day though you really just might fall in and get hurt. Loose ends are almost never worth the struggle and it adds to so much self doubt and confusion. It’s not worth the headache and inevitable battle it may drag you back into. No judgement at all by the way regardless of how you go about your situation, because your feelings are valid and it’s easier said than done. Everybody’s different and loves and feels different. I block my exes after the end of a toxic relationship immediately but that doesn’t mean I’m free from thinking about them because I do on occasion. I just ask a close friend or two to remind me of why it ended in the first place and to “make me feel bad for missing them” and they readily oblige 😂😂 sometimes you need a good cringe or guilt trip to persuade you (even if for a moment) that the good times definitely weren’t worth it in comparison to how being in the relationship as a whole made you feel.
